statement: The numbers 1, 2, 3, ... are written in rows. Row 1 has one number, row 2 has two numbers, row 3 has three numbers, and so on. So row 1 is 1, row 2 is 2, 3, row 3 is 4, 5, 6 and row 4 is 7, 8, 9, 10. What is the first number in row 12?

choices.misconception: I found the first number of row 11 instead of row 12.
I found the last number of row 11 and forgot to move on to the next number.
I found the last number of row 12 instead of the first.
I worked out 11 x 12 = 132 for the numbers in rows 1 to 11, forgetting to halve it, then added 1.

hints: How many numbers are written before row 12 starts?
Rows 1 to 11 hold 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + 11 numbers altogether. Row 12 starts with the very next number.
To add 1 + 2 + ... + 11, pair 1 with 11, 2 with 10, and so on: each pair makes 12.

solutions.reliable: The last number in each row equals how many numbers have been written so far. Rows 1 to 11 hold 1 + 2 + ... + 11 numbers. Pairing 1 with 11, 2 with 10, 3 with 9, 4 with 8 and 5 with 7 makes five pairs of 12, with 6 left over: 60 + 6 = 66. So row 11 ends with 66, and row 12 starts with 67. Check against the rows shown: row 4 should start after 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 numbers, at 7, and it does. The transferable idea: in a table that grows row by row, the last number of a row is the running total of the row lengths.
solutions.elegant: Look at the ends of the rows: 1, 3, 6, 10, ... The gaps between them are 2, 3, 4, ..., so keep adding: 15, 21, 28, 36, 45, 55, 66. That is the end of row 11, so row 12 starts at 67.

whyOnTest: Table and grid patterns test finding a rule for where a row starts or ends, instead of writing out the whole table.
